zhu-long-ort-2008.authors: Zhu, X.-G.; Long, S. P.; Ort, D. R.
zhu-long-ort-2008.title: What is the maximum efficiency with which photosynthesis can convert solar energy into biomass?
zhu-long-ort-2008.note: Theoretical maxima: 4.6 % for C3 plants (30 °C, 380 ppm CO2) and 6 % for C4 plants.

blankenship-2011.authors: Blankenship, R. E.; Tiede, D. M.; Barber, J.; et al.
blankenship-2011.title: Comparing photosynthetic and photovoltaic efficiencies and recognizing the potential for improvement
blankenship-2011.note: Annually, PV-driven electrolysis beats photosynthesis; best short-term photosynthetic yields come within a factor of 2–3.

ort-durham-2012.title: Comparing light-conversion efficiency of plants and manmade solar cells
ort-durham-2012.note: Plain-language summary of Blankenship et al. (2011): crop plants convert about 1 percent of solar energy; PV-driven electrolysis about 10 percent annually.

fao-bioenergy-future.authors: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
fao-bioenergy-future.title: Chapter 7: The future of renewable biological energy systems
fao-bioenergy-future.container: FAO, Renewable biological systems for alternative sustainable energy production (Agricultural Services Bulletin 128)
fao-bioenergy-future.note: States that agricultural and forestry efficiencies seldom exceed 1 % of solar input converted to a recoverable product.

nobel-chemistry-1961.title: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1961: Melvin Calvin

fargione-2008.authors: Fargione, J.; Hill, J.; Tilman, D.; Polasky, S.; Hawthorne, P.
fargione-2008.title: Land clearing and the biofuel carbon debt

ipcc-ar6-wg3-ch7.authors: Nabuurs, G.-J.; Mrabet, R.; Abu Hatab, A.; et al. (IPCC)
ipcc-ar6-wg3-ch7.title: Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses (AFOLU). In: Climate Change 2022: Mitigation of Climate Change, Working Group III contribution to the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report, Chapter 7
ipcc-ar6-wg3-ch7.note: BECCS technical CDR potential 5.9 (0.5–11.3) GtCO2/yr, medium confidence; poorly planned biomass deployment may conflict with sustainability, high confidence.

wiki-ethanol-brazil.title: Ethanol fuel in Brazil
wiki-ethanol-brazil.note: Encyclopedia used as a last resort for the 1975 Pró-Álcool start date and the 2003 flex-fuel launch.

wiki-beccs.title: Bioenergy with carbon capture and storage
wiki-beccs.note: Encyclopedia used as a last resort for the Illinois Industrial CCS dates (pilot from 2011, commercial phase from 2017) and the count of operating large-scale BECCS projects (Global CCS Institute 2024).

kalogirou-2004.title: Solar thermal collectors and applications
kalogirou-2004.container: Progress in Energy and Combustion Science 30(3), 231–295
kalogirou-2004.note: History section: Shuman and Boys' Meadi (Egypt) pumping plant, operating 1913, 62 m parabolic cylinders, 1200 m², 37–45 kW, shut down 1915.

doe-csp-mirrors-2001.authors: U.S. Department of Energy; National Renewable Energy Laboratory
doe-csp-mirrors-2001.title: Concentrating Solar Power: Energy from Mirrors
doe-csp-mirrors-2001.note: Solar One (10 MW) operated 1982–1988; Solar Two (10 MW) 1996–1999 with molten nitrate salt at about 565 °C and 3 h storage.

solarpaces-segs-i.title: CSP Projects database: Solar Electric Generating Station I
solarpaces-segs-i.note: 13.8 MW parabolic trough, Daggett CA, start 1984; decommissioned.

solarpaces-csp-db.title: Concentrating Solar Power Projects database (all projects, CSV export)
solarpaces-csp-db.note: SEGS I–IX capacities (13.8 + 6 × 30 + 2 × 80 MW ≈ 354 MW); tower, trough and Fresnel projects worldwide. SolarPACES states the database has not been updated since October 2023.

solarpaces-gemasolar.title: CSP Projects database: Gemasolar Thermosolar Plant / Solar TRES
solarpaces-gemasolar.note: 20 MW tower, 2011, two-tank direct molten salt storage of 15 h, 2650 heliostats of 120 m², 140 m tower, salt 290 °C cold / 565 °C hot.

solarpaces-noor-iii.title: CSP Projects database: NOOR III
solarpaces-noor-iii.note: 150 MW molten-salt tower, Ouarzazate, Morocco, start 2018, 7 h storage, 247 m tower.

pge-ivanpah-2025.title: PG&E agrees to end power purchases from Ivanpah solar project to save customers money
pge-ivanpah-2025.note: Announced 17 January 2025, pending CPUC approval; plant began generating in 2014; PG&E contracted units 1 and 3; deliveries end from 2026.

iha-outlook-2026.title: 2026 World Hydropower Outlook
iha-outlook-2026.note: Launch release, 24 June 2026: pumped storage 201 GW at the end of 2025 after a record 11.7 GW added in 2025; 243 GW under construction and a 621 GW pipeline; total hydropower 1,469 GW; generation 4,495 TWh; 'the world's dominant form of large-scale energy storage'.

iha-outlook-2025.title: 2025 World Hydropower Outlook
iha-outlook-2025.note: States that pumped storage accounts for more than 90 % of the world's energy storage; 189 GW installed at the end of 2024.

ren21-gsr-2024-storage.title: Renewables 2024 Global Status Report: Energy Systems and Infrastructure, Energy storage
ren21-gsr-2024-storage.note: 2023: pumped storage 179 GW; battery storage 55.7 GW after 120 % growth; batteries were 83 % of utility-scale storage capacity additions.

umich-css-storage-2026.authors: Center for Sustainable Systems, University of Michigan
umich-css-storage-2026.title: U.S. Grid Energy Storage Factsheet (Pub. No. CSS15-17)
umich-css-storage-2026.note: The Rocky River pumped storage plant (1929) was the first large-scale US energy store; pumped hydro round-trip efficiency 70–85 %.

pnnl-storage-2019.authors: Mongird, K.; Viswanathan, V.; Balducci, P.; Alam, J.; Fotedar, V.; Koritarov, V.; Hadjerioua, B.
pnnl-storage-2019.title: Energy Storage Technology and Cost Characterization Report (PNNL-28866)
pnnl-storage-2019.note: Round-trip efficiency: pumped hydro 0.80, CAES 0.52, vanadium flow 0.675 (2018) to 0.70; lithium-ion 0.83 (2025 estimate). Response time: batteries about 1 s; pumped hydro 5–70 s up to minutes depending on mode.

pnnl-storage-2022.authors: Viswanathan, V.; Mongird, K.; Franks, R.; Li, X.; Sprenkle, V.; Baxter, R.
pnnl-storage-2022.title: 2022 Grid Energy Storage Technology Cost and Performance Assessment (PNNL-33283)
pnnl-storage-2022.container: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory for the U.S. DOE, August 2022
pnnl-storage-2022.note: Installed cost of 100 MW systems in 2021 US$/kWh: Li-ion LFP 4 h ≈ 385; vanadium flow 10 h ≈ 385; pumped hydro 10 h ≈ 263; CAES 10 h ≈ 122.

nrel-battery-cost-2025.authors: Cole, W.; Ramasamy, V.; Turan, M.
nrel-battery-cost-2025.title: Cost Projections for Utility-Scale Battery Storage: 2025 Update (NREL/TP-6A40-93281)
nrel-battery-cost-2025.note: 4-hour utility-scale battery about 334 US$/kWh in 2024 (2025 projections 295–350); round-trip efficiency taken as 85 %. Projected 2025 cost: low 295, mid 321, high 350 US$/kWh; 15-year life.

inl-hydrogen-2023.authors: Balliet, W. H.; Casteel, M. (Idaho National Laboratory)
inl-hydrogen-2023.title: Bidirectional Hydrogen Storage: Technology Strategy Assessment (Storage Innovations 2030)
inl-hydrogen-2023.note: Baseline round-trip efficiency 31 % for a system with a 73 % electrolyser and a 51 % fuel cell.

nobel-chemistry-2019.title: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2019: Goodenough, Whittingham and Yoshino, for the development of lithium-ion batteries

caiso-duck-2016.title: What the duck curve tells us about managing a green grid (Fast Facts)
caiso-duck-2016.note: Projected spring net-load ramp: an additional 13,000 MW within approximately three hours (by 2020).

nrel-duck-2015.authors: Denholm, P.; Brinkman, G.; Jorgenson, J. (National Renewable Energy Laboratory)
nrel-duck-2015.title: Overgeneration from Solar Energy in California: A Field Guide to the Duck Chart (NREL/TP-6A20-65023)
nrel-duck-2015.note: Without more flexibility, solar at about 20 % of annual energy could push marginal curtailment above 30 %.

eia-duck-2023.title: As solar capacity grows, duck curves are getting deeper in California (Today in Energy, 21 June 2023)
eia-duck-2023.note: CAISO battery capacity grew from 0.2 GW (2018) to 4.9 GW (April 2023).

doe-duck-2017.title: Confronting the duck curve: how to address over-generation of solar energy

kroposki-2017.authors: Kroposki, B.; Johnson, B.; Zhang, Y.; et al.
kroposki-2017.title: Achieving a 100% renewable grid: operating electric power systems with extremely high levels of variable renewable energy

lin-2020-grid-forming.authors: Lin, Y.; Eto, J.; Johnson, B.; Flicker, J.; Lasseter, R.; Villegas Pico, H.; Seo, G.; Pierre, B.; Ellis, A.
lin-2020-grid-forming.title: Research Roadmap on Grid-Forming Inverters (NREL/TP-5D00-73476)
lin-2020-grid-forming.note: Inverter controls today are predominantly grid-following; the transition to grid-forming will be gradual.

dorfler-gross-2023.title: Control of low-inertia power systems
dorfler-gross-2023.container: Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems 6, 415–445

wiki-hvdc.title: High-voltage direct current
wiki-hvdc.note: Encyclopedia used as a last resort: Gotland link 1954 (100 kV, 20 MW, citing Hingorani 1996, IEEE Spectrum); 1,100 kV, 3,300 km, 12 GW link in China completed 2019; HVDC losses about 3.5 % per 1000 km (citing EU JRC 2017).

wiki-utility-frequency.title: Utility frequency
wiki-utility-frequency.note: Encyclopedia used as a last resort: grid codes (2017) asked equipment to ride through a RoCoF of 1–4 Hz/s.

wiki-pumped-storage.title: Pumped-storage hydroelectricity
wiki-pumped-storage.note: Encyclopedia used as a last resort: first pumped storage at Engeweiher near Schaffhausen, Switzerland, 1907; first US use 1930 near New Milford, Connecticut (Rocky River).

wiki-li-ion.title: Lithium-ion battery
wiki-li-ion.note: Encyclopedia used as a last resort for dates: Whittingham 1974, Goodenough LiCoO2 1980, Yoshino 1985, Sony commercial cells 1991.

wiki-hornsdale.title: Hornsdale Power Reserve
wiki-hornsdale.note: Encyclopedia used as a last resort: commissioned 1 December 2017 at 100 MW / 129 MWh, the largest lithium-ion battery in the world at the time; expanded to 150 MW / 193.5 MWh in 2020.

wiki-segs.title: Solar Energy Generating Systems
wiki-segs.note: Encyclopedia used as a last resort: nine trough plants totalling 354 MW in the Mojave, the first commissioned in 1984; the world's largest solar thermal facility until Ivanpah (2014); most units retired by 2021.

shn-engeweiher-2026.title: Stromversorgung unter Druck: Die Batterie von 1909 zeigt den Weg in die Zukunft
shn-engeweiher-2026.note: Local newspaper, 2 September 2026, quoting the operator SH Power: the Engeweiher above Schaffhausen was built in 1909 and is the oldest storage plant still operating in Switzerland. (German Wikipedia gives construction 1907–1909.)

asme-rocky-river.title: Rocky River Hydroelectric Station: a National Historic Mechanical Engineering Landmark (landmark brochure)
asme-rocky-river.note: Construction began 1926 and was completed in 1928; 'the first large-scale pumped-storage development in the United States'; 'the first known pumped-storage development was in Zurich, Switzerland, in 1882, which was hydro-mechanical until 1891'. Designated 13 September 1980.

nobel-chemistry-2019-popular.authors: Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences / Nobel Prize Outreach
nobel-chemistry-2019-popular.title: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2019: popular information
nobel-chemistry-2019-popular.note: Whittingham's first functional lithium battery in the early 1970s; Goodenough's cobalt oxide cathode published 1980; Yoshino's lithium-ion battery 1985; 'In 1991, a major Japanese electronics company started selling the first lithium-ion batteries' (the company, Sony, is not named).

arena-hornsdale-2019.title: World's biggest battery grows and gains new powers
arena-hornsdale-2019.note: Government agency, 29 November 2019: 'the world's biggest battery'; original 100 MW / 129 MWh commissioned December 2017; expansion of 50 MW / 64.5 MWh to 193.5 MWh.

hpr-faq.title: Frequently asked questions
hpr-faq.note: Operator: 100 MW / 129 MWh construction completed 1 December 2017; 50 MW / 64.5 MWh expansion completed in the first half of 2020.

ieee-gotland-milestone.title: Milestone-Proposal: Gotland HVDC Link (approved milestone, docket 2015-05)
ieee-gotland-milestone.note: World's first commercial HVDC transmission link and first submarine HVDC cable: commissioned March 1954, 100 kV, 20 MW, 96 km mass-impregnated cable from mainland Sweden to Gotland.

hitachi-changji-guquan.title: Changji–Guquan UHVDC link (customer story)
hitachi-changji-guquan.note: Supplier: ±1,100 kV, 12,000 MW, over 3,000 km from Xinjiang to Anhui, commissioned 2019; world records for voltage, capacity and distance.

eia-icf-hvdc-2018.authors: ICF Incorporated, for the U.S. Energy Information Administration
eia-icf-hvdc-2018.title: Assessing HVDC Transmission for Impacts of Non-Dispatchable Generation
eia-icf-hvdc-2018.note: June 2018: HVDC line losses roughly 3.5 % per 1000 km against 6.7 % for comparable AC lines at similar voltage; converter stations lose 0.6–1 % of the power delivered; total HVDC losses typically 30–40 % lower than AC on long lines.

ghd-aemc-rocof-2022.authors: GHD Pty Ltd, for the Australian Energy Market Commission
ghd-aemc-rocof-2022.title: System Rate of Change of Frequency: a GHD survey of international views
ghd-aemc-rocof-2022.note: 18 November 2022. Generator RoCoF withstand requirements: Ireland and Great Britain ±1 Hz/s (500 ms); ENTSO-E ±2 Hz/s (500 ms); Chile ±2 Hz/s; Australia NEM/WEM ideal ±4 Hz/s over 250 ms (minimum ±2 Hz/s).

fapesp-proalcool-2016.title: Proálcool, one of Brazil's major science and technology based achievements
fapesp-proalcool-2016.note: News agency of the São Paulo Research Foundation, 21 December 2016: 'Proálcool, the National Fuel Alcohol Program created by government decree in November 1975'.

goldemberg-2008.title: The Brazilian biofuels industry
goldemberg-2008.note: 'The introduction of flex-fuel motors in Brazil, in 2003, ...'

adm-decatur-2021.title: ADM announces successful completion of one million metric ton carbon capture and storage project (press release)
adm-decatur-2021.note: Operator, 19 May 2021: the Illinois Basin–Decatur Project stored one million tonnes of CO2 from the Decatur ethanol plant over three years; the Illinois Industrial CCS project began injecting in April 2017; more than 3.4 million tonnes stored by the two projects together.

bioenergyintl-iccs-2017.title: ADM starts commercial-scale CCS at Decatur ethanol plant
bioenergyintl-iccs-2017.note: Trade press, 20 April 2017: Illinois Industrial CCS began operations on 7 April 2017, able to handle up to 2,000 tonnes of CO2 a day; the earlier Illinois Basin–Decatur Project ran 2011–2014 and stored about a million tonnes over three years; DOE contributed US$141 million.
